question: Ozone layer thickness is measured in:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dobson Unit**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The thickness of the ozone layer is measured in Dobson units (DU):
 
• A DU is a unit of measurement for the total amount of ozone in a vertical column of air above the Earth's surface. It's a convenient way to describe how much ozone would be in a column if it were squeezed into a single layer.
 
• One DU is equal to the amount of ozone that would form a layer 1 mm thick at sea level if compressed at Standard Temperature and Pressure (STP).
 
• What is the average ozone layer thickness?
 
• The average amount of ozone in the atmosphere is about 300 DU, which is equivalent to a layer 3 mm thick.
 
• British meteorologist G. M. B. Dobson developed a spectrophotometer that could measure stratospheric ozone from the ground.
 
• He also established a worldwide network of ozone monitoring stations between 1928 and 1958.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Decibels are a unit of measurement used to express the intensity of sound or the power level of an electrical signal on a logarithmic scale.
 
• Del Unit
 
 
• This term isn't standard or widely recognized in scientific contexts.
 
• You may mean something like a "Dalton (Da)" (used for atomic mass) or a "unit related to mechanics". 
 
 
 
• Sievert (Sv)
 
 
• The Sievert is the SI unit of equivalent radiation dose.
 
• It measures the health effect of ionizing radiation on the human body
 
 
 
• Formula:
 
 
• Sievert=absorbed dose (Gray)×radiation weighting factor Sievert=absorbed dose (Gray)×radiation weighting factor
